title: "R3. Who to ask"
description: "Who to ask, communities of practice, and closing a skills gap."
---


| If you need | Ask |
|---|---|
| Advice on your assurance level, or a level dispute resolved | The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead |
| A critical friend for your analysis | Your team lead in the first instance |
| Advice on official statistics | The Lead Official for Statistics |
| Business Critical registration | The Data Science, Statistics and AI team, which holds the register |
| Information governance advice, or help with personal data | The central information governance mailbox, which takes the request and starts a data protection impact assessment. Ask before the work starts, not at sign-off |
| Help with analytical code, testing or reproducibility | The owners of the [Analytical Code Assurance Playbook](https://nhsbsa-data-analytics.github.io/nhsbsa-analytical-code-assurance-playbook) |

: Kinds of help you may need and who to ask for each

Each row names a role or a team rather than a person, so that a change of post holder is not a
change to this playbook. Who currently holds each one is in the governance and management framework.

**Two of the rows rest on something outside this playbook.** The Lead Official for Statistics is
NHSBSA's title for the role the Code of Practice for Statistics requires of any producer of
official statistics, and calls the Head of Profession for Statistics. The Data Science,
Statistics and AI team holds the register, which is why Business Critical registration goes
there. Who holds each post is in the governance and management framework.

**The information governance mailbox is the route, and this page does not carry its address.**
Ask your team lead, or write to the analytical assurance mailbox below and ask to be routed.

If you cannot work out who to approach, start with your team lead. If that does not settle it,
write to [analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk](mailto:analyticalassurance@nhsbsa.nhs.uk). That
mailbox covers this playbook, the Analytical Assurance Decision Tool and the Business Critical
templates, and will point you at the right person for anything else.

## Communities of practice

Collaboration is worth seeking at the start of analysis rather than when you are stuck. It gives
access to skills and knowledge held outside your immediate team, avoids duplication and wasted
effort, avoids conflicting results, and brings a wider range of professional perspectives.

### Coffee and Coding

A monthly, hands-on session lasting 45 minutes to an hour, in which colleagues share a skill and
everyone gets to run the code themselves. It has run since May 2021 and materials from every session
are published at
[the Coffee and Coding page on GitHub](https://github.com/nhsbsa-data-analytics/coffee-and-coding).

Past sessions have covered R and Python from scratch, the Open Data Portal API, R Markdown and
official statistics, accessible spreadsheets, and data visualisation. You do not need to be a
confident coder to attend, and you do not need to present to benefit.

For joining details, ask your team lead or the Data Science, Statistics and AI team.

## When the work needs a new skill {#when-the-work-needs-a-skill-you-do-not-have}


Whoever assigns a piece of work has to give it to people with the skills, information and tools it
requires. The obligation sits as much on whoever does the work as on whoever assigns it. That is a
statement about the work, not a judgement about the analyst.

There is no single analytical training catalogue to point you at. Follow these two steps.

**Say so early.** A skills gap found at scoping is a conversation about who else is involved, what
training is needed, or whether the deadline moves. The same gap found at assurance is a finding
against the analysis. Raise it with your team lead, and if it is not resolved there, with the
Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead using the routes above.

**Record it if it is not closed.** Where the work goes ahead without the skill the assurance level
assumes, that is a limitation of the analysis. Record it, and put it in the quality assurance
statement, the same as any other limitation. See
[deciding your assurance level](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd) and
[Phase 4, delivery, communication and sign-off](../04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.qmd).

Two frameworks help with the wider question of whether NHSBSA has the capability it needs, rather
than with a single piece of work:

| Framework | What it assesses |
|---|---|
| [Statistical Practice Capability Framework](https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/), Office for Statistics Regulation | How an organisation is developing its statistical practice against Trustworthiness, Quality and Value.<br><br>It is in development and being trialled with producer bodies, so it is a way of looking at NHSBSA, not a standard NHSBSA is held to |
| [Government Analytical Evaluation Capabilities Framework](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-magenta-book), a Magenta Book supplementary guide | The competences an evaluation team needs, and how to judge whether it has them |

: Capability frameworks and what each assesses
